target: Si Budi selalu punya cerita lucu setiap kali kami berkumpul.
english: Budi always has a funny story every time we get together.
grammar: Si before a name marks warmth among friends: si Budi ≈ 'good old Budi'. Casual only — never for elders.

target: Kemarin si kecil menangis karena balonnya terbang ke atas pohon.
english: Yesterday the little one cried because her balloon flew up into a tree.
grammar: Si + adjective names someone by a trait: si kecil = the little one, si sulung = the eldest.

target: Di kantor, si pendiam itu ternyata paling pandai bercerita.
english: At the office, the quiet one turns out to be the best at telling stories.

target: Si sulung suka mengatur adik-adiknya seperti ibu kedua.
english: The eldest likes to boss her younger siblings around like a second mother.

target: Setiap sore si bungsu menunggu ayah pulang di depan pagar.
english: Every afternoon the youngest waits for dad to come home in front of the gate.

target: Kucing kami dipanggil si belang karena bulunya hitam putih.
english: Our cat is called Spots because its fur is black and white.
grammar: Pets often get si + trait as a name: si belang = the stripey one, si putih = the white one.

target: Waktu SD, teman-teman memanggil saya si kacamata.
english: In elementary school, my friends called me 'glasses'.

target: Si Tono datang paling akhir, tetapi ceritanya paling panjang.
english: Tono arrived last, but his story was the longest.

target: Semua orang di kampung kenal si penjual bakso itu.
english: Everyone in the village knows that meatball seller.

target: Si pemalu di kelas kami sekarang menjadi pembawa acara terkenal.
english: The shy one in our class is now a famous host.

target: Si rambut panjang itu dulu sering mampir ke warung nenek saya.
english: That long-haired one used to often drop by my grandma's food stall.

target: Anak-anak menyebut anjing itu si galak karena suka menggonggong.
english: The kids call that dog 'the fierce one' because it likes to bark.

target: Si Sari lagi-lagi lupa membawa kunci rumahnya sendiri.
english: Sari has yet again forgotten to bring her own house key.
grammar: Lagi-lagi = 'yet again' (mild exasperation): Lagi-lagi hujan = It's raining yet again.

target: Dulu kami takut pada si satpam, padahal dia sebenarnya ramah sekali.
english: We used to be scared of the security guard, even though he was actually very friendly.

target: Si juara kelas itu sekarang mengajar matematika di sekolah kami.
english: That class champion now teaches mathematics at our school.

target: Katanya dulu di sini ada pasar malam setiap akhir pekan.
english: They say there used to be a night market here every weekend.
grammar: Katanya = 'they say / I heard' — marks retold info: Katanya dia pindah = I heard he moved.

target: Dia tidak datang kemarin, katanya motornya mogok di tengah jalan.
english: He didn't come yesterday; he said his motorbike broke down in the middle of the road.

target: Kata Ibu, dulu ayah pernah tersesat di kota ini selama dua hari.
english: According to Mom, Dad once got lost in this city for two days.
grammar: Kata + person = 'according to': Kata Ibu, ... = Mom says ... Katanya alone = generic hearsay.

target: Ceritanya dia mau memberi kejutan, tetapi kuenya jatuh di tangga.
english: The story goes that he wanted to give a surprise, but the cake fell on the stairs.
grammar: Ceritanya = 'the story goes' — opens an anecdote: Ceritanya mau kejutan = supposedly a surprise was planned.

target: Kata tetangga, rumah kosong itu akhirnya laku juga bulan lalu.
english: According to the neighbors, that empty house finally sold last month.

target: Katanya paman pernah bertemu orang terkenal di pasar ikan.
english: They say Uncle once met a famous person at the fish market.

target: Ceritanya kami mau mendaki gunung, tetapi semua orang bangun kesiangan.
english: The story was that we were going to hike the mountain, but everyone woke up late.

target: Katanya begitu, tetapi saya belum pernah melihatnya sendiri.
english: That's what they say, but I've never seen it myself.

target: Menurut cerita kakek, sumur tua itu tidak pernah kering.
english: According to grandpa's story, that old well has never run dry.

target: Katanya antrean di sana panjang, ternyata kami dilayani cepat sekali.
english: They said the line there was long; it turned out we were served very quickly.

target: Teman saya bercerita bahwa dia pernah salah masuk rumah tetangga.
english: My friend told me that he once went into the neighbor's house by mistake.

target: Katanya film itu seram sekali, jadi kami menonton sambil menutup mata.
english: They say that movie is really scary, so we watched while covering our eyes.

target: Ceritanya panjang, pokoknya kami baru sampai rumah jam dua pagi.
english: It's a long story; anyway, we didn't get home until two in the morning.
grammar: Pokoknya = 'anyway, bottom line' — skips the details: Pokoknya kami selamat = Anyway, we made it.

target: Kata sopir angkot, jalan ke pasar ditutup karena ada pawai.
english: According to the angkot driver, the road to the market is closed because there's a parade.

target: Katanya dia menang lomba masak, ternyata itu hanya mimpi.
english: He said he won a cooking contest; it turned out it was only a dream.

target: Setiap kali kami berkumpul, om suka mengulang cerita masa mudanya.
english: Every time we get together, my uncle likes to repeat stories from his youth.

target: Katanya resep sambal nenek tidak pernah diberikan kepada siapa pun.
english: They say grandma's sambal recipe has never been given to anyone.

target: Ceritanya aku mau berhemat bulan ini, tetapi ada diskon besar di mana-mana.
english: The story was I was going to save money this month, but there were big discounts everywhere.

target: Kabarnya pasangan itu bertemu pertama kali di halte bus.
english: Word has it that couple first met at a bus stop.
grammar: Kabarnya = 'word has it' — rumor from no one in particular: Kabarnya mereka pindah = Word is they moved.

target: Semua itu baru kata orang, belum tentu benar kejadiannya.
english: All that is just hearsay; what happened isn't necessarily true.
grammar: Kata orang = 'people say', hearsay: baru kata orang = it's only hearsay, not confirmed.

target: Saya sedang menonton berita, tiba-tiba listrik di rumah padam.
english: I was watching the news when suddenly the electricity at home went out.
grammar: Tiba-tiba = sudden, you see it happen; tahu-tahu = you only notice the result: Tahu-tahu sudah malam.

target: Tahu-tahu sudah jam dua belas dan tugas saya belum selesai.
english: Before I knew it, it was already twelve o'clock and my assignment wasn't finished.
grammar: Tahu-tahu = 'before you know it': Tahu-tahu sudah pagi = Suddenly it was morning (time slipped by).

target: Kami sedang asyik mengobrol, tiba-tiba hujan turun deras sekali.
english: We were deep in conversation when suddenly it started raining very hard.

target: Anak itu tadi ada di sebelah saya, tahu-tahu dia sudah di atas pohon.
english: That kid was next to me just now; next thing I knew he was already up the tree.

target: Tiba-tiba semua lampu mati, dan kami menyalakan lilin sambil melanjutkan cerita.
english: Suddenly all the lights went out, and we lit candles while continuing the story.

target: Saya menutup mata sebentar di bus, tahu-tahu kami sudah sampai terminal.
english: I closed my eyes for a moment on the bus; next thing I knew we had already reached the terminal.

target: Dia tiba-tiba berdiri dan berteriak bahwa dia lupa mematikan kompor.
english: She suddenly stood up and shouted that she forgot to turn off the stove.

target: Tahu-tahu gelas di ujung meja sudah pecah di lantai, padahal tidak ada orang.
english: Next thing we knew, the glass at the edge of the table had shattered on the floor, even though no one was there.

target: Waktu itu kami sedang berfoto bersama, tiba-tiba seekor monyet mengambil topi ayah.
english: At that moment we were taking a photo together, when suddenly a monkey grabbed dad's hat.

target: Saya meninggalkan gorengan sebentar di dapur, tahu-tahu sudah habis dimakan kucing.
english: I left the fried snacks in the kitchen for a moment; next thing I knew the cat had eaten them all.

target: Tiba-tiba ban sepeda saya kempis, padahal perjalanan masih jauh sekali.
english: Suddenly my bicycle tire went flat, even though the journey was still very long.

target: Kemarin sore langit masih cerah, tahu-tahu malamnya air hujan masuk ke teras.
english: Yesterday afternoon the sky was still clear; before we knew it, that night rainwater came onto the porch.

target: Adik tiba-tiba menangis keras karena es krimnya jatuh ke pasir.
english: My little brother suddenly cried loudly because his ice cream fell into the sand.

target: Kami baru bicara tentang Pak Tono, tahu-tahu beliau muncul di pintu.
english: We had just been talking about Mr. Tono; next thing we knew he appeared at the door.
grammar: Beliau = respectful 'he/she' for elders and bosses: Beliau sudah datang = He (respected) has arrived.

target: Tiba-tiba ada suara keras dari dapur, ternyata tumpukan panci jatuh.
english: Suddenly there was a loud sound from the kitchen; it turned out a stack of pots had fallen.

target: Saya menaruh kue itu di meja, tahu-tahu tinggal bungkusnya saja.
english: I put the cake on the table; next thing I knew only the wrapper was left.
grammar: Tinggal here = 'only ... left': tinggal bungkusnya = only the wrapper is left; tinggal satu = one left.

target: Musim hujan datang tiba-tiba tahun ini, lebih cepat daripada biasanya.
english: The rainy season arrived suddenly this year, earlier than usual.

target: Dulu dia sering datang ke warung ini, tahu-tahu sekarang sudah menjadi orang terkenal.
english: He used to come to this food stall often; before we knew it, he has now become famous.

target: Kami lama memilih tempat makan, ujung-ujungnya kami memasak di rumah.
english: We took a long time choosing a place to eat; in the end we cooked at home.
grammar: Ujung-ujungnya = 'in the end (predictably)': Ujung-ujungnya saya yang membayar = In the end, of course, I paid.

target: Dia bilang mau diet, ujung-ujungnya dia pesan dua porsi bakso.
english: He said he wanted to diet; in the end he ordered two portions of meatballs.

target: Setiap liburan kami mau bangun pagi, ujung-ujungnya semua bangun siang.
english: Every holiday we intend to wake up early; in the end everyone wakes up late.

target: Rapatnya panjang sekali, ujung-ujungnya keputusannya tetap sama seperti kemarin.
english: The meeting was very long; in the end the decision stayed the same as yesterday.

target: Anak-anak minta hewan peliharaan, ujung-ujungnya ibu yang memberi makan setiap hari.
english: The kids asked for a pet; in the end it's mom who feeds it every day.

target: Kami membandingkan harga di lima toko, ujung-ujungnya kembali ke toko pertama.
english: We compared prices at five shops; in the end we went back to the first shop.

target: Katanya dia cuma mau melihat-lihat, ujung-ujungnya dia pulang membawa tiga kantong belanja.
english: She said she just wanted to look around; in the end she went home carrying three shopping bags.
grammar: Doubling a verb makes it aimless/casual: melihat-lihat = just browsing, jalan-jalan = stroll around.

target: Mereka bertengkar soal arah jalan, ujung-ujungnya dua-duanya salah.
english: They argued about which way to go; in the end both of them were wrong.
grammar: Dua-duanya = both of them: dua-duanya salah = both are wrong; tiga-tiganya = all three.

target: Saya coba memperbaiki keran sendiri, ujung-ujungnya kami tetap memanggil tukang.
english: I tried to fix the tap myself; in the end we still called a repairman.

target: Ujung-ujungnya semua cerita kakek selalu kembali ke masa mudanya di desa.
english: In the end, all of grandpa's stories always come back to his youth in the village.

target: Untung saya sempat memotret pelangi itu sebelum hilang di balik awan.
english: Luckily I managed to photograph that rainbow before it disappeared behind the clouds.
grammar: Sempat = managed to fit it in: sempat memotret = got the chance to snap it before it was too late.

target: Tadi pagi dia hanya sempat minum teh sebelum berangkat kerja.
english: This morning he only had time to drink tea before leaving for work.

target: Kami sempat bingung mencari pintu keluar di mal sebesar itu.
english: We were briefly confused looking for the exit in a mall that big.
grammar: Sempat + feeling = briefly felt it: sempat bingung = was confused for a moment (then it passed).

target: Sebelum pindah ke luar kota, mereka sempat berpamitan ke semua tetangga.
english: Before moving out of town, they had the chance to say goodbye to all the neighbors.

target: Saya sempat berpikir kami tersesat, ternyata hotelnya memang di gang kecil itu.
english: I briefly thought we were lost; it turned out the hotel really was in that little alley.

target: Untung kamu sempat mencatat nomor teleponnya sebelum ponselmu mati.
english: Luckily you managed to write down his phone number before your phone died.

target: Dia sempat bekerja sebagai pemandu wisata waktu tinggal di Bali.
english: He worked for a while as a tour guide when he lived in Bali.
grammar: Sempat also = 'at some point did': sempat bekerja di Bali = worked in Bali for a time.

target: Kemarin kami tidak sempat mampir karena jalanan macet parah.
english: Yesterday we didn't get a chance to stop by because the traffic was terribly jammed.

target: Sebelum pesawat lepas landas, saya sempat mengirim pesan kepada ibu.
english: Before the plane took off, I managed to send a message to my mother.

target: Anak-anak sempat bermain hujan sebentar sebelum disuruh masuk oleh neneknya.
english: The kids got to play in the rain for a bit before being told to come inside by their grandma.

target: Saya sempat malu karena memanggil orang asing dengan nama teman saya.
english: I was embarrassed for a moment because I called a stranger by my friend's name.

target: Kami sempat mengira acaranya batal karena panggungnya masih kosong.
english: We briefly thought the event was canceled because the stage was still empty.

target: Untung dia sempat menangkap gelas itu sebelum jatuh ke lantai.
english: Luckily he managed to catch that glass before it fell to the floor.

target: Waktu antre di kasir, saya sempat lupa nomor PIN kartu sendiri.
english: While queuing at the checkout, I briefly forgot my own card's PIN number.

target: Dia sempat tinggal setahun di rumah kami waktu kuliah dulu.
english: He lived at our house for a year back when he was in college.

target: Disuruh mematikan televisi, adik malah menyalakan semua lampu di rumah.
english: Told to turn off the TV, my little brother instead turned on all the lights in the house.
grammar: Malah = does the opposite of expected: disuruh tidur, dia malah menonton = told to sleep, he watches instead.

target: Obat itu tidak mengurangi batuk saya, malah membuat saya tidur seharian.
english: That medicine didn't reduce my cough; instead it made me sleep all day.

target: Kami datang untuk menghibur dia, dia malah menghibur kami dengan leluconnya.
english: We came to cheer him up; instead he cheered us up with his jokes.

target: Sudah diberi jalan lebih dekat, dia malah memilih jalan memutar.
english: He'd already been given a shorter route; instead he chose the long way around.

target: Hujan sudah berhenti, tetapi banjir di jalan kami malah makin tinggi.
english: The rain has stopped, but the flood on our street is actually getting higher.

target: Saya yang salah, tetapi dia malah meminta maaf lebih dulu.
english: I was the one in the wrong, but he apologized first instead.

target: Niatnya menghemat uang, kami malah membeli oleh-oleh untuk satu kampung.
english: The intention was to save money; instead we bought souvenirs for a whole village.

target: Ban mobil sudah diganti, sekarang mesinnya malah berbunyi aneh.
english: The car tire has been replaced; now the engine is making a strange noise instead.

target: Kami pindah supaya lebih tenang, di rumah baru malah lebih ramai.
english: We moved so things would be calmer; at the new house it's actually noisier.

target: Adik disuruh menjaga kue, dia malah menghabiskan setengahnya sendiri.
english: Little brother was told to guard the cake; instead he finished half of it himself.

target: Saya bertanya arah kepada orang itu, dia malah ikut bingung.
english: I asked that person for directions; instead he got confused too.

target: Sudah memakai peta, kami malah makin jauh dari tempat acara.
english: Even though we were using a map, we instead got farther from the venue.

target: Waktu saya sampai, dia kaget dan bilang, "Lho, kamu bukannya di Bandung?"
english: When I arrived, she was startled and said, "Huh, aren't you supposed to be in Bandung?"
grammar: Lho = spoken surprise particle, heard everywhere: 'Lho, kamu di sini?' Understand it — no need to use it.

target: Penjaga warung tertawa dan bertanya, "Kok kamu kembali lagi, ada yang ketinggalan?"
english: The stall keeper laughed and asked, "How come you're back again — did you leave something behind?"
grammar: Kok (spoken) = 'how come?': 'Kok belum tidur?' = How come you're not asleep? Kenapa is the neutral word.

target: Gara-gara salah baca jadwal, saya menunggu bus yang tidak pernah datang.
english: Because I misread the schedule, I waited for a bus that never came.
grammar: Gara-gara = 'all because of' (blaming tone): gara-gara macet = all because of the traffic jam.

target: Kemarin saya salah naik angkot dan baru sadar setelah setengah jam.
english: Yesterday I took the wrong angkot and only realized after half an hour.
grammar: Salah + verb = did it wrong: salah naik = took the wrong one, salah kirim = sent it to the wrong person.

target: Dia salah kirim pesan cinta ke grup keluarga besar.
english: He sent a love message to the extended-family group by mistake.

target: Saya menyapa orang asing di mal karena saya kira dia teman kantor.
english: I greeted a stranger at the mall because I thought he was a coworker.

target: Sepatu saya tertukar dengan sepatu tamu lain di acara pernikahan.
english: My shoes got swapped with another guest's shoes at the wedding.
grammar: Ter- often means 'by accident': tertukar = got swapped, tertinggal = got left behind.

target: Kami terkunci di luar rumah, padahal makanan masih di atas kompor.
english: We were locked out of the house, even though food was still on the stove.

target: Saya baru sadar kaus saya terbalik setelah seharian jalan-jalan.
english: I only realized my T-shirt was inside out after strolling around all day.

target: Waktu mati lampu, saya menyikat gigi dengan krim wajah.
english: During the blackout, I brushed my teeth with face cream.

target: Ceritanya saya mau tampil rapi, ternyata saya memakai kaus kaki yang berbeda warna.
english: The story was I wanted to look neat; it turned out I was wearing socks of different colors.

target: Saya tertidur di kereta dan terbangun tiga stasiun setelah tujuan saya.
english: I fell asleep on the train and woke up three stations past my destination.

target: Untungnya ada penumpang yang membangunkan saya sebelum kereta kembali berangkat.
english: Luckily there was a passenger who woke me before the train departed again.
grammar: Untungnya = 'luckily' — introduces the rescue: Untungnya ada yang menolong = Luckily someone helped.

target: Dompet saya tertinggal di warung, untungnya penjualnya jujur dan menyimpannya.
english: My wallet got left behind at the food stall; luckily the seller was honest and kept it.

target: Saya pernah membalas lambaian orang yang ternyata melambai ke orang di belakang saya.
english: I once waved back at someone who turned out to be waving at the person behind me.
grammar: Membalas = return/reply: membalas lambaian = wave back, membalas pesan = reply to a message.

target: Pas saya mau membayar, mesin kasir mati dan antrean makin panjang.
english: Right when I was about to pay, the register died and the line got longer.
grammar: Pas (spoken) = 'right when / just as': pas saya mau membayar = just as I was about to pay.

target: Saya bicara satu jam di telepon dengan semangat, rupanya sambungannya sudah lama terputus.
english: I talked on the phone enthusiastically for an hour; apparently the connection had long been cut.
grammar: Rupanya = 'apparently, so it turns out' — the moment truth clicks: Rupanya dia sudah tahu = Turns out he knew.

target: Sampai-sampai tetangga ikut keluar karena mendengar kami tertawa terlalu keras.
english: So much so that the neighbors came out too, because they heard us laughing too loudly.
grammar: Sampai-sampai = 'so much so that': sampai-sampai dia menangis = to the point that he cried.

target: Kisah ayah jatuh ke kolam ikan masih ditertawakan sampai sekarang.
english: The story of dad falling into the fish pond is still laughed about to this day.

target: Kami tertawa sampai sakit perut mendengar cerita masa kecil paman.
english: We laughed until our stomachs hurt hearing uncle's childhood stories.

target: Dia menahan tawa waktu melihat bos salah memakai kacamata orang lain.
english: He held back laughter when he saw the boss mistakenly put on someone else's glasses.

target: Anehnya, kunci yang hilang itu muncul lagi di dalam kulkas.
english: Strangely, the lost key turned up again inside the fridge.
grammar: Adjective + -nya opens a comment: Anehnya = the strange thing is..., Lucunya = the funny part is...

target: Lucunya, kami berdua membeli kado yang sama untuk orang yang sama.
english: The funny thing is, the two of us bought the same gift for the same person.
grammar: Ber- + number = a group of people: kami berdua = the two of us, mereka bertiga = the three of them.

target: Pokoknya malam itu semua rencana kami berantakan, tetapi kami pulang sambil tertawa.
english: Anyway, that night all our plans fell apart, but we went home laughing.

target: Saya pura-pura tenang, padahal saya baru saja menumpahkan kopi di laporan bos.
english: I pretended to be calm, even though I had just spilled coffee on the boss's report.
grammar: Pura-pura = to pretend: pura-pura tenang = pretend to be calm, pura-pura tidur = pretend to sleep.

target: Sopir taksi itu terus bercerita sepanjang jalan sampai kami lupa soal macet.
english: That taxi driver kept telling stories the whole way until we forgot about the traffic jam.

target: Waktu kecil, saya percaya cerita kakak bahwa semangka bisa tumbuh di perut.
english: When I was little, I believed my brother's story that watermelons could grow in your stomach.

target: Setiap ada tamu, ikan dalam cerita ayah makin lama makin besar.
english: Every time there are guests, the fish in dad's story gets bigger and bigger.
grammar: Makin lama makin X = more and more X over time: makin lama makin besar = keeps getting bigger.

target: Kami salah masuk gedung dan ikut rapat kantor orang selama sepuluh menit.
english: We entered the wrong building and sat in on someone else's office meeting for ten minutes.

target: Ternyata sepanjang wawancara ada sisa sambal di ujung bibir saya.
english: It turned out that throughout the interview there was leftover chili sauce on the corner of my lips.

target: Saya tidak menyangka kebohongan kecil itu akan diingat teman-teman bertahun-tahun.
english: I never expected that little lie would be remembered by my friends for years.
grammar: Tidak menyangka = never expected: Saya tidak menyangka dia datang = I didn't expect him to come.

target: Gara-gara tertawa di saat hening, saya menjadi pusat perhatian satu ruangan.
english: Because I laughed during a silent moment, I became the center of attention for the whole room.

target: Sekarang setiap kali lewat jembatan itu, kami pasti ingat kejadian topi ayah.
english: Now every time we pass that bridge, we always remember the incident with dad's hat.

target: Ceritakan lagi bagian waktu kamu melompati pagar karena takut anjing kecil itu.
english: Tell again the part when you jumped over the fence because you were afraid of that little dog.
grammar: Commands drop meN-: Ceritakan! = Tell it! In statements the full form returns: Dia menceritakan...

target: Dari semua cerita liburan kami, salah naik kapal ke pulau lain tetap juara.
english: Of all our vacation stories, taking the wrong boat to another island is still the champion.
